reports.headline: Viking Fleet — 2026-08-27 (Montauk)
reports.body: Capt Dave reports another great day on the Viking Starship. They started down the beach out of the tide with very good fishing — all large and jumbo porgies — then headed offshore to a sea bass spot with plenty of sea bass but only a handful of keepers and some fluke. They finished east of the lighthouse at anchor on a mix of medium porgies and small sea bass. First place pool winner was Errol Burke from Bronx, NY with a 2.5 lb porgy.

reports.headline: Jingles Bait and Tackle — 2026-08-27 (Beach Haven)
reports.body: Jingles’ Aug. 27 daily Beach Haven report said it was a mostly sunny, warm morning, wind from the south at about 11 mph, surf calm with 1–2 foot waves (3–4 oz to hold), Beach Haven water about 75°, air 79° heading to 80°, and the bay calm at 74.8°. They still have one more month for fluke season and were hearing of some bigger fluke being caught — the majority still shorts but some keepers coming in too; early in the week Mark Bartlett brought in a 3.2 lb, 20.25-inch keeper. Best bet was out at the reefs, though they got word of a nice-sized fluke just caught out back in the bay. On the surf there has been a lot of fluke action but again mostly shorts, with more kingfish and anglers also reporting cocktail blues.

reports.headline: Jones/Debbs Inlet Saltwater Fishing Report 2026-08-27
reports.body: Had a nice day outside yesterday. Found cocktail blues south of the Pink Hotel blitzing in the morning, then had non-stop action on the McAllister most of the day with fluke, sea bass and porgies. Took home one huge porgy for the table and we were rewarded with a nice 25 inch fluke. We ran to the AB mid-day hoping for something different, but the bite was slower so we returned to McAllister. We did get to see two nice sized whales there. All in all a great day on the ocean. Tight lines, Capt. Larry

reports.headline: New England Bluefin Tuna 2026-08-27
reports.body: Another beautiful day today on Cape Cod. Left Harwichport Saquatucket harbor at 5:00 am this morning. Steamed out to the sword in look for a rec bluefin. Got on scene found the life whales and porpoise around. Several other not were out there giant fishing spread out among the fleet. A couple of giants were caught out there. But for the couple of guys who were trolling I didn't see any hook up in the troll. At about 9:00 am the fleet pushed further East of the sword. Not quite sure if they found better life over that way but I did not make the move. But a fun day overall with calm seas. Would have just been a nice bonus if I found that one dumb tuna to hit. Next time for sure!!!

reports.headline: Big Mohawk — 2026-08-26 (Belmar)
reports.body: Big Mohawk’s Aug. 26 fishing report said a great day back out on the fluke grounds, with lots of limits around the boat today and high hooks a double limit. Morning was best, a steady pick of keepers coming up; the afternoon bite slowed down to a pick. With the slow drift this morning, anglers casting spinning rods with jigs did best. A few pool fish in the 5 lb range. They thanked everyone for fishing hard, said they will take a pass on tomorrow due to high winds, and will be back at it Friday sailing 6 a.m., book online or come down, walk-ons welcome.

reports.headline: Cape May County Herald Fishing Line — 2026-08-26 (Cape May)
reports.body: Mark Robbins’ Aug. 26 Fishing Line (Cape May County Herald) said dog-days heat has slowed the pace but fish are still being caught. Captain Bob of Full Ahead Sport Fishing reported boat-limit fluke with many keepers 20 inches-plus and around 4 pounds from several areas. Captain Chuck on the Sea Star III reported good fluke action (some days hurt by a lack of drift), with keepers, shorts, limits, plus sea bass and triggerfish in the mix; pool winners on that boat were all fluke from 2.5 to 4.1 pounds. Miss Chris, Captain Mike at the wheel, has been catching flounder and triggerfish. Cape May Bait and Tackle reported croakers to 16 inches from the local beaches on bloodworms or Fishbites, short flounder with an occasional keeper (a 20-incher recently), bigger flounder on the reefs on spearing and Gulp, and small bluefish starting to show. Captain Adam on the Atlantic Adventure has had flounder, triggerfish, sea bass, and ling on local reefs and some deepwater trips. Stalker Fishing Charters (Captain Skip) is running backwater striper and flounder trips and ocean trips for fluke and other reef fish.

reports.headline: J&J Sports / Patchogue Fishing Center — 2026-08-24 (Patchogue)
reports.body: Pablo Salinas’s Aug. 24 J&J Sports report said September marks the start of the highly anticipated fall run, which most anglers regard as the best part of the season, with large blues, trophy-sized striped bass, and albies flooding local waters. The bass and bluefish bite in the fall is unmatched because of the influx of baitfish, and during the fall the inlets, bays, and open beaches are all great places to catch bass and blues. With warmer water, fishing has been most active during incoming tides; back-bay patterns that simulate snappers and spearing are the key, and he said don’t be surprised to catch larger fluke on hard plastics, even at night. Local docks are producing fluke, blowfish, kingfish and snappers; fluke fishing has been pretty good at Moriches Coast Guard Station (shorts in the mix); there has been a surprising run of weakfish in the Great South Bay; blues are starting to pick up at Moriches and Shinnecock inlets on incoming tides; and the porgy bite continued to hold strong.
reports.species: striped bass, bluefish, false albacore, fluke, blowfish, kingfish, weakfish, porgy, black sea bass, bonito

reports.headline: J&B Tackle Co. — 2026-08-24 (Niantic)
reports.body: Tim Driscoll’s Aug. 24 J&B Tackle report said fluke and black sea bass fishing remains good throughout the area, with anglers continuing to pick through plenty of short fish to land some keepers; Black Point, Niantic Bay, and Two Tree Channel have all produced keeper fluke and black sea bass this week, with reports of larger fish coming from the Montauk area. Striped bass fishing continues to be best around dawn and in the evening, and live-lining eels at night remains one of the most productive ways to target the biggest striped bass. The biggest inshore news this week is that bonito were at Watch Hill on Friday — the JB Tackle boat was in the area and reported fish everywhere, with no other boats around — and he said look for these fish to spread out along the south side of Fishers Island as the week progresses. Early morning continues to be the best time to target bonito, although anglers can catch bones throughout the day; use small peanut-style epoxy jigs or fast-retrieved metals, watch for working birds and fast-moving blitzes, and like false albacore, bonito also tend to favor choppy water. Offshore, fishing from Fishtails to East and West Atlantis remains very good; Haabs continues to be the starting point for nearshore tuna fishing, and jigging produced better results than trolling this week.
reports.species: fluke, black sea bass, striped bass, bonito, false albacore, tuna

reports.headline: The Saltwater Edge — 2026-08-21 (Middletown)
reports.body: Tyler Richman’s Aug. 21 Saltwater Edge forecast said the fall run is starting to kick off in Rhode Island, with shoals of baitfish making their way to the oceanfront from the salt ponds, rivers, and estuaries. There have been bonito and even a handful of Spanish mackerel caught over the past couple of weeks, with albies hopefully not far behind; the bluefin bite on the midshore grounds is picking up nicely, with fish well dispersed across a very large area, and there have been whispers of some yellowfin midshore, though not yet consistent. Inshore, the striped bass bite is good, but the ridiculous numbers of sharks make it really difficult; the bottom fishing is also good but a bit lackluster compared to previous years — there is no shortage of short fluke and black sea bass, but consistently finding quality keepers is another story.

reports.headline: Yankee Fleet — 2026-08-20 (Gloucester)
reports.body: Yankee Fleet said customers and crew have been enjoying great weather the last week or so. Full day trips have been good; the Yankee Clipper is doing a great job avoiding the dogfish, with occasional surprise stops but a lot of trips at very low dogfish numbers (1-20 for a boat full of anglers). Haddock and pollock are coming up, and some of the better trips did very well on the pollock. Half days are killing it — one dogfish all week, loads of reds, hake/whiting regularly coming over, and some big cusk. Marine life has been exciting recently as well, with dolphins, whales, and sunfish seen regularly on the ride in or out and during fishing.
reports.species: haddock, pollock, dogfish, redfish, hake, whiting, cusk

reports.headline: Yankee Fleet — 2026-08-20 (Gloucester)
reports.body: Yankee Fleet posted this recap on 20 August of the Platts overnight on the Yankee Star, 10/11 August. They reported fantastic fishing and a good night bite: mixed bag of haddock, pollock, cusk, and big squid for an hour or so. After sunrise and a tide change they drifted the rest of the trip; daylight fishing was great, with nonstop pollock, a fair amount of haddock with some 7 lbs+, cusk/redfish mixed in, and some anglers fishing the whole trip with zero dogfish. Fish counts ranged from 25 to 50+, and the end of the trip was giving anglers some monster pollock.
reports.species: haddock, pollock, cusk, squid, redfish, dogfish

reports.headline: Grumpy's Tackle — 2026-08-20 (Seaside Park)
reports.body: John Budish’s Aug. 20 Grumpy’s Tackle report (Seaside Park, N.J.) said the fishing report hasn’t changed much from the last one: the fluke are still biting in the surf, there are some bluefish around, mostly near the inlet and mostly on the small side, and the Spanish mackerel and bonito are being very cooperative. In the boats it’s still lots of short fluke in the quest to find one to invite home for dinner; he told anglers to keep an eye out for Spanish mackerel or bonito popping up, and wherever they fish to keep epoxy jigs or small metals handy.
